condition: lifelong attention deficit symptoms at work refractory to 8 weeks of daily primary-care attention medication
level_rationale: Childhood-onset sustained attention deficits that continue to impair keeping up with daily work tasks despite 8 weeks of daily primary-care attention pharmacotherapy indicate treatment-refractory adult attention-deficit symptoms warranting psychiatrist evaluation for diagnostic confirmation and specialist medication optimization, whereas developing a resting heart rate of 180 beats per minute while taking daily focus medication indicates acute sympathomimetic tachyarrhythmia requiring immediate emergency department assessment and cardiac monitoring.

reference_facts.text: Has had trouble staying focused or sustained attention deficits since childhood
Has taken daily attention or focus medication from primary care for 8 weeks
Still has difficulty keeping up with tasks at work

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain working-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + sourced laziness self-attribution belief clause (-att, Stralin 2024) + single-fact focus-medication tachyarrhythmia escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (childhood-onset difficulty staying focused, ongoing 8-week daily focus medication from primary care, and ongoing difficulty keeping up with work tasks) with a 2-word span difference (24 vs 26 words) and zero stated negatives. Following reviewer_notes Rule A's medication-effect precedent (r11-001), replacing f3 with 'now have a resting heart rate of 180 beats a minute' directly motivates mentioning the ongoing 8-week daily focus medication while escalating care unambiguously from psychiatrist optimization (level 3) to emergency department evaluation for acute sympathomimetic tachyarrhythmia (level 4).
